utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you continue, please, with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The witness is Senad Muslimovic whose direct evidence is continuing. MR. SENAD MUSLIMOVIC, recalled

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated, Mr. Muslimovic. You are still under oath, sir. Mr. Tieger, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Muslimovic, when we adjourned on Friday you were describing the second beating you suffered involving the man whose photograph you selected. You had reached the point, I believe, of describing how while on the floor of the hangar building you had been held standing against a demper tyre while the group practised blows, mostly kicks, on you. Did the attack continue until you lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In translation]: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you were again aware of where you were, what position were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my knees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you being beating at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not much, but there was a blow here and there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you were on the floor of the hangar in that position, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was kneeling. My arms were forward and somebody held my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You made a gesture with your arm pulling it back. Was your head pulled back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just referring to the gesture you made with your hand as you described what happened. Did that indicate that your head or hair was grabbed and your head pulled back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. The person who was holding my head also held a knife at my throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was the person who was holding your head and holding a knife to your throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person I recognised in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At that moment were you essentially waiting for your throat to be cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure, what else could I expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. I had a man standing in front of me, "Don't, leave him for the end", but, nevertheless, I felt on my throat a burn. I guess he must have passed with a knife over my throat. I did not know at that moment whether I had been cut or not, and immediately after that I felt that somebody grabbed my ear and the same feeling as on the throat I had at that moment too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the man who was holding your ear the same man who had held the knife to your throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he say anything as he held your ear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when this, I do not know what to call him, the man with the white belt, he said, "Well, I have at least to cut off his ear".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The man holding me, the man who passed his knife against, across my throat and the one who grabbed my ear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, and he said that "I have to at least cut off his ear" to the man in the white belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To another man and to me, surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same. I felt that sting on my ear and immediately after that I felt a stab in my left shoulder and I felt terrible pain, and it was something like when somebody exercised pressure and starts twirling something, but it did not last long. Then another stab, I did not know what was happening, but I felt pain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when the knife was drawn across your throat and across your ear, were those parts of your body actually cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. You described how there was a feeling of the knife coming across your throat and also a similar feeling against your ear. With whatever portion of the knife was drawn against your throat and ear, did it actually cut your throat, that portion of your throat or ear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later on I realised that he did not, but it was a burning feeling on my throat, and this pressure of the knife against my throat must have been stronger and that is why I felt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: However, was your shoulder actually stabbed twice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you were stabbed twice by the man whose picture you selected, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, beating, regular beating, I received a blow in the back which was somewhat stronger so I staggered forward and then this was followed by a series of blows from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did those blows continue until you again lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you next experience as you began to regain your consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I felt my legs in the air being lifted. I thought that it was simply because I was unconscious that that is what happened, but shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As your awareness of where you were improved, did you realise that you were actually hanging in the air upside-down by your feet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately, how far off the ground were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my hands were -- I could still touch the floor. I do not know how high but my hands could still touch the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what you were hanging from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened while you were hanging in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again a series of blows ensued from the left and from the right with feet, with batons, until I fainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you were next aware of where you were, what position were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was lying down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you being beaten at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you lay there on the ground, what were you able to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a person who had dragged a young man whom I knew from sight. We were not acquaintances. He was also beaten and hit from the left and from the right, cutting him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any words being spoken while he was being cut and attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first words I heard, the first words, when he appeared within my vision was, "Jasko, what are you doing in Benkovac?" and I heard the same person, "I do not know, I have done nothing, Dule, cross my heart, I know nothing".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the person who had been addressed as "Jasko" when he was cut was he stabbed or cut in a different fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him stabbed. He was being cut, sliced as if once one slices chops.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see who was cutting him in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same person who did it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The man whose picture you selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the man had been cut, as you indicated, did you see anything else happen to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some black liquid was poured over him, I do not know what it could be, it looked black to me -- probably oil, but I could not establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the next thing that happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a short while I heard behind my back, but it must have been from a distance, "Look, he's still alive". So after a very short while, I think, beatings from the back started again and continued and I lost consciousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember where you were after the point of that beating and after you lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Posture, my eyes were turned towards the entrance door. I was lying down. I could see that, that area, the entrance into that area, into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point did you end up in one of the oil pits or canals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember how I got there, only know how I came out. After those blows I somehow found myself in one of the -- in a canal, I do not know how.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know how you got out of the canal? Were you assisted by the soldiers who were beating you to pull you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same person who beat me, the one with the white belt, helped me get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to WC to wash myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the man in the white belt or anyone else in the WC say anything to you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was washing, the water was dirty, my hands were bloody, and I heard behind my back, "If he manages to the dormitory, he will be alive for today at least".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Having heard that, did you somehow manage to get back to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same person who kept calling me out and take me out and took me out from the canal grabbed me by the shoulder, turned me and said, "Scram, scram so they do not see you again", and naturally I moved towards the room and I got there, how, I do not know, somebody may know it, but in those moments I felt nothing. I only thought I had to get to that room. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, what injuries did you suffer during this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Knife stab in two places, right shoulder, cut, cuts along my arms, and naturally blows with the batons which do not leave fractures, but leave another effect, pain, blows in the head. My jaw was broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were your feet cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that on the instep of your foot, the middle portion at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The medium part of the foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know when that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On this occasion do you recall what the man whose photograph you selected was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he clean shaven or did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was unkempt, he was not shaven. He did not have a beard. He simply looked like a man who had not shaven for two or three days. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the times you saw him in camp did you notice or observe anything distinctive or noticeable about the way he walked or moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He walked like a bear. He moved like a bear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Although it may be difficult to imitate, can you indicate perhaps from your chair what kind of a movement that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try. It is very difficult because that gait is only his. (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you sir. Nothing further, your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Before you begin, Mr. Kay, we will continue until 1 o'clock when we normally take our lunch break since we began late this morning because we were handling another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Muslimovic, the first matter I want to ask you about is this, and it concerns whether you have seen any photographs of the accused in this case in the newspapers or television. Last week you told us that you had not seen any photographs of the man accused in this courtroom, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I have not seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have been living in a place -- would I be right to say that it is in Europe? I do not want to know the country but just whether you have been living in Europe since you left Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand, were you referring to before or after?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the conflict and after you left this area, over the last few years perhaps, would it be right to say that you have been living in Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The place where you live has television, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are newspapers available to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never. I do not read papers and I never bought them either before or after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you see newspapers around perhaps when you travel into the town or see other people reading newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what interested in least in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It may not interest you, but I just want to know whether you are a person who has never seen a newspaper over the last two or three years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have seen newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the events that happened to you in Omarska, have you taken an interest in what has been happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I knew everything and I was not interested in anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were not tempted out of curiosity to see what was happening in relation to allegations against Serbian people concerning those matters that were happening in your former country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said once, I was not interested in that. I wanted to forget it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, what I suggest to you is this, that before you saw that photograph album that was presented to you by an investigator for the Prosecution, you had, in fact, seen pictures of the arrest of Dusko Tadic in Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what you would like to say, but I say I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have had contacts with Muslim people from your region or from Bosnia-Herzegovina in the last couple of years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you talked about what happened to you and what was being done about the arrest of Serb people with fellow Muslims who have had to leave Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said once before that this was of no interest to me any more. I wanted to forget it. Those were difficult moments and I do not want to remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is not quite as simple as that though, as something you wanted to forget, because you have made yourself available as a witness for the Prosecution to talk about these matters today, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On an occasion earlier this year you made yourself available so that a statement was taken from you where you discussed matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true, but, well, probably people know how many times they have asked, they ask me to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When that photograph album was shown to you this year, can you remember what the date was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was of no interest to me so I do not know. I think it was May. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your statement was taken in March of this year, the precise date in March does not matter, but when that statement was taken from you in March, was that the occasion when the photograph album was also shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the photograph album, in fact, shown to you after that statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I talked three or four times to them and only then was I shown the photographic album.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the time that you came to look at that photograph album was nearly four years since those events had happened to you in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if it was three and a half or four, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was almost four years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you know that, I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you were looking at was a photograph of what size?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell it how much in centimetres. I could show it like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could hold your fingers up to the Court so that the Bench may see what you have indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated) A centimetre, up or down, but around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a black and white photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That photograph was not the whole body of a man, but from his shoulders upwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was only looking at the head. I was not interested in the shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, essentially, a photograph that just showed the face of the man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a photograph of a man without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A man whose hair was cut fairly short?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not say it was all that short.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. You see, what I suggest to you is that you, perhaps, have not told us the truth about this matter, that you did not look at any photographs of Dusko Tadic that have been seen on the world news and in the newspapers of the country where you had been living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the question. I do not know what you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is, and it is for to you accept or deny, that it is not true when you have told us that you did not see any photographs of Dusko Tadic before you looked at that photograph album this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So your recollection of the man that you saw on those occasions in Omarska are recollections of someone that you did not see any image of between the period that you left Omarska and the time that you looked at the photograph album, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The number of occasions that you say you saw this man in Omarska amount to some four occasions, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All total about five or six times, maybe seven, maybe six, maybe five, five, six or seven. I do not know the exact count, nobody was counting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I said four occasions because I was considering the evidence that you gave us at the end of last week that referred to two collisions which are the incidents that you have described and two other occasions that you saw him at the white house and by the kitchen in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a mistake. I never saw him in the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you told us at the end of last week was that you saw him near the white house when you were looking from a window in the room in which you were detained.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is something else. There is a big difference between near the white house and in the white house. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that you saw him near the kitchen or by the kitchen on an occasion when you were going for lunch?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am sorry. I have to object. Counsel is not correctly stating the record which indicates ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Give us a page and line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Page 25, 25, lines 15 through 16, or you can start at 14, 15, "How many times did you see him by the kitchen?" Answer: "About two times". Then line 19: "How many times did you see him by the white house?" Line 20: "Also about two times".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have the transcript? You should have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have taken it from the transcript, your Honour, because your Honour will recollect that the first matter which is related to a beating after the interrogation arises when it is alleged that the defendant was by the white house.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I guess the controversy that occurred was when you said you had seen him in the white house, the witness said "no" and you said, "That is what you had testified to" and he said, "No, there is a difference between in the white house and near the white house -- at the white house".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It says "in front of the white house", yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Not "in the white house".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So do you accept Mr. Tieger's objection at least that you are not properly recounting the testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think it is right that the witness, of course, made the distinction himself and there was, perhaps, no need for an objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Except you are moving on to something else now, I gather.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was two-fold. Counsel also suggested to the witness that he had said he only saw the man once by the kitchen and once by the white house. The testimony clearly indicates, consistent with what the witness has said today, that he saw him twice by the kitchen and then saw him about two times near the white house when he was looking from the window. I think that is also a clear representation of the transcript. Counsel did not have it correct when he asked the question in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Re-ask your question, Mr. Kay. I am afraid I am lost. I thought there was a distinction of how many times. I thought you had said four times and the witness had said, "No, that is not so, it was more like six or seven times".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know where in the transcript we can resolve that issue. It has not been addressed by Mr. Tieger. So if you will ask your next question, let us see what we can do about getting it straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I will do is deal with the matter in another way. I know the Court has a copy of the transcript anyway. (To the witness): What I would like to question you about now is that others, you say, pointed out the man to you as being Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question again. Please can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before you were in Omarska you did not know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had spent no time with that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Others pointed to a man and said, "That was Dusko Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can tell us the occasion when others pointed him out to you? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were going to the lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were not in the room that you were being held in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were not looking from a window in the hangar building and others pointed him out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The first occasion you say that you were beaten by Dusko Tadic, that occurred after you had had an interrogation in the investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew the man known as "Dule". I did not know that his last name was "Tadic".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I asked you was, the first occasion you said that you were beaten by the man, it was after you had been questioned in the investigation centre in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was during your stay in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe five or six days after I arrived in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that you saw that man with others in the area in front of the white house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many others were with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six, maybe seven. I did not have time to count.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were they doing? Were they sitting or standing at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were sitting, some were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time of the day it was that your interrogation had finished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you leaving the investigation centre on your own or with a guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it the habit that when you were moving around the camp you were required to look down at the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you told us on Friday was that you stole a look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You stole a look to see the group of men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any reason why you did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are looking to be saved. There were still good men around who could help.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had just received a beating during your interrogation in the investigation centre, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your questioning had finished and you were being returned to the room in the hangar, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. They did not return me. They were beating me along.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there other guards with you, other than the one escorting you from the investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only one who was escorting me and beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because you used the plural "they" were beating you and I wanted to know who else was beating you other than that guard you were with when you were moving from the investigation centre back to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe that is what I said, but I referred to everything when I was escorted down from the investigation, and I did not even know where they were they leading me, they were taking me and they were going left and right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I am talking to you about now is that time when you say you stole a look to see the men on the grass area near the white house. At that stage you were being beaten, were you, by one man or more than one man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I said -- I am repeating -- there were four men beating me when I was interrogated and I was led back by one man. So I called it the plural because that day I was beaten by multiple men, and so there were four men who beat me during the interrogation and then one man as he was escorting me back. I do not know what else to say, to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where those men were in front of the white house, they appeared to have no particular business with you, is that right? They had not been involved in your investigation earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not. Those men were not upstairs where I was interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For some reason you were chased by them, you told us. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how, if you can say "chased", if that is how you say it, it is all right. I was, I sped up, they followed me. There was no running involved. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it the whole group of some six or seven men who then confronted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The group you had seen on the grass area in front of the white house, was it that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The group of men you had seen in front of the white house, was it the whole group who confronted you and beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was not the whole group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were these men armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were, some were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say it was the man called Dusko Tadic who grabbed you by the hair, can you recollect how he was dressed, what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same uniform as he was wearing that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could describe that to us, as to what that uniform was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me, it was the camouflage uniform. I do not know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect if there was a belt on that uniform and, if so, what colour of belt it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there was a belt, but I do not recall the colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From what you describe you were pulled by your hair from behind, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were being forced to kiss the badge on a beret of a man who was in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was forced to but I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So for some reason you chose not to do that when you were under threat and fear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Somehow you were able to escape from where you were being held with those men around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not audible to me. I did not hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In what way? I do not know how, but I was saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember the names of any other people who were within that group of men who were attacking you in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Saponja, and the gentleman from the picture, the others I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Saponja was involved on this occasion, was he, this first occasion that you had the beating in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he involved in the second occasion as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You also referred at the end of last week to someone called Dusko Kecman (sic)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No never, not even then. If you can pronounce the man exactly, then I will -- it is not Kecmar, it is not -- I do not know those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Kecema, which I have recorded here as K-E-C-E-M-A?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is -- that is something else, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he there on this first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We just checked the transcript. Judge Stephen has brought the transcript. It seems that when the witness testified he said, "I recognise Kecema, Dusko or perhaps I thought he could be the one who could perhaps help me". So it appears that Kecema and Dusko are two different people. Is that how you understood it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is the practice of using of what we would call the surname first with a first name afterwards. If your Honour will see down at line 32, the understanding of the question at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is good. Thank you, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. (To the witness): But you told us last week that Kecema was there on this first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kecema was present on the grass. I remember those two men. Those who beat me along the way, I did not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking you now about the time that you were being held, and you have told the Court that it was the man in the photograph who was present there at that time. I am interested in that time when you were beaten by this group, having come into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see you are interested in time. I was never interested in time. All I know it was afternoon. That is all. I did not write textbooks there or minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Confronted, though, with that group and being beaten in that way, how were you able to escape?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that was asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will sustain -- Mr. Kay, I recall that you asked it and I can recall that the witness kind of chuckled. He said, "I do not know, I got away".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I did ask it before -- your Honour is quite right -- and I have been trying to orientate the witness into the position where this beating ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will sustain the objection. It has been asked and answered. He says he does not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. (To the witness): There we are. So that it is clear, what I suggest to you is this, that in fact you did not recognise Dusko Tadic as being present when this beating took place, if it took place at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what you think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I turn now then to the second incident that you allege involved the man in the photograph? When you were called out of the room, was that by a guard or one of the group who was eventually involved in giving you the beating down in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That came from the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were taken down from the room you were in into the hangar by a guard or was it by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody escorted me. I was called out. I came out. The guard who stood at the door moved a little bit away and sat down. So I walked down the stairs. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many people were down in the hangar who made up this group that attacked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven, eight, 10. Not less than seven. There must have been more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, if I can ask you this, can you identify any of the people who were present there at that time other than the man you say was in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it is just the man in the photograph is the one you identify as being part of that group, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the man with a white belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know the name of the man with the white belt or can you identify him by any other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know the name. I only remember his white slings, that is all, and heavy blows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, this is a beating that took place when you lost consciousness several times, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The effect on you must have caused you to have become very disorientated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every now and then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you lose consciousness and then return to consciousness, was that an experience that caused you to have difficulty with understanding what exactly was happening to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I did not understand the question completely. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you lost your consciousness and eventually regained it, were you, in fact, in a state of confusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To an extent that you were unsure of what was happening around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am quite positive about what was going on around me -- more than positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, you see, what I suggest to you is that photograph has been shown to you and you knew already by other sources what Dusko Tadic looked like, and you were determined to identify him ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- and the circumstances you were in on that day were such that you have no clear recollection of what the man looked like amongst the others who were attacking you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you went through the same thing, you would also remember it quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just have one point of clarification, your Honour, and I do not know how to do that without, I guess, announcing in advance that I think we will need a redaction from the record. So, if it is permissible to the Court, I will proceed despite that necessity. The question -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It depends upon how long you will proceed because if we need a redaction, do we need to go back and you need to give us a time for the redaction? Can we handle that first? Am I following you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think the question will elicit a response which will require a redaction, just to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Fine. You proceed. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): I think there was some confusion earlier, sir -- I just have one question for you -- you were asked whether or not you had been living in Europe since the time of the war and since leaving the area of the conflict. Is it not true that you emigrated to a country in (redacted) where you have been living since the time of your emigration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent a very short part of that in Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my mind, Slovenia, Austria and all the rest are Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. But you actually emigrated to a country in (redacted) where you have been living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I wanted to clarify, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Muslimovic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, you are permanently excused. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you for inviting me. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann and Mr. Tieger, who will handle the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Armin Kenjar. MR. ARMIN KENJAR, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, would you take the oath there that has been handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, can you tell the Court your name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Armin Kenjar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what year were you born?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does Kamicani border Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it primarily an area consisting of homes and houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Kozarac where the shops, cafes and stores of the local area were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So was central Kozarac the area where people from Kamicani went to town when they needed to shop and such?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The people from Kamicani considered Kozarac their town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you sometimes say that you were from Kamicani and sometimes say you were from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your occupation before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked in the carpenters shop that we had there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your duties in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a rank. I was with the Engineers Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When did you serve with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you did serve, did you return home to the Kozarac area to work as a carpenter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a long time, many years, since I was a child. He used to be my idol once. I passed by his coffee bar. I went to this gym where he practised. I looked through the window many times when a child.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was he your idol as a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he was a karateist, he was the trainer, coacher. He was the best. We all thought him the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you grew up and became a young adult, did you continue to see him and know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Every day, every week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would the two of you wave and greet each other as you passed by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, regularly when we pass each other by, to greet each other, if we know each other, then to say "hello".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic have a noticeable or distinctive way of walking or moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was rather characteristic, an athletic, like a cowboy, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us what that looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Approximately four to five months before the war, were you called up as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your duties as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, I was to be in the security of the police station in Kozarac. Then it was checkpoints around Kozarac and in Kozarac itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the checkpoints, was that some form of traffic control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, traffic control and control of weapons, if somebody was in illegal possession of some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did all nationalities, including Serbs, or did both Serbs and Muslims work at the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of your duties as a reserve policeman, did you become aware of an incident involving the Serbian Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard something about it and then I looked up the book that was on the table, a book of applications.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that a log book in which incidents or events were recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, something of the sort that is all complaints were put on, were noted down in that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see that incident recorded in the log book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did the log book indicate about that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a short description that Mr. Tadic had been seen in the vicinity of the church with canisters of petrol and with the probable intent of setting the church on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, where were you when the attack on Kozarac began on May 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were at home asleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had you worked the night before and is that why you were asleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did a family member wake you up to tell you that ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- the war had started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started for Kamicani, in the direction of the fire, gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you try to travel to Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After going to the area of Kamicani, did you then try to go to the police headquarters in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you trying to find out what was happening or what you could do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if you could clear up, where did he start from?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour. (To the witness): Where exactly was your home, Mr. Kenjar, and where were you going? I think the confusion is you said you were going to Kamicani and the Court is aware that your home was in Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was -- I started for the Local Commune building in Kamicani. We called, that part around that centre we called Kamicani, we also belonged in Kamicani, that part where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you got to the police headquarters in Kozarac, was anyone there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no-one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you eventually go to a shelter which had been built by your brother and his neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I returned towards the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there many women and children there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From that time until May 29th did you spend your time going from the shelter and bringing blankets and food to refugees in the Brdjani area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was bringing food to the refugees, the civilians, where I did not spend any time in the shelter. I was helping everyone I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also bring food to the Muslim defence line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many men were there at the defence line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 50. There were one group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the foothill of Menkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were those people armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were very poorly armed. Some had an automatic rifle, some had the old rifle, M48, some of those had some hand-made weapons. They were very poorly armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point before May 29th did you decide to make an effort to escape from the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you want to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Eventually what point did you hope to reach, what point of safety?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you intend to stay in Bosanska Dubica or go on after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we thought of somehow getting across to Croatia from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say "we", did you go with a friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had a friend along.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you and your friend went towards Bosanska Dubica, were you trying to avoid Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were avoiding them in every way we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you spend the night in the forest, for example, in that effort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we spent one night, until the daybreak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next morning were you and your friend seen and captured by Serb forces in Mostanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were noticed and caught.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mostanica is near Bosanska Dubica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostanica is near Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you were seized, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken to the prison in Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you placed in a cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, before that we were interrogated and then returned to the cell. Then we were put in that cell in which we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was a Serb also put in that cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. At some point while you were held in the prison in Bosanska Dubica, was a Serbian man put in your cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a Serb was brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was that Serbian man put in the cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he had defended Muslims, because he did not hate Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After he was put in the cell, were you or your friend or any other Muslims in the cell told to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had to beat him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you forced to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who forced you to do that, first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of those guards who were around there told me to hit him. I said, "Why should I? The man is not responsible for anything. I have no reason".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you initially declined to hit him, what did the guard say or do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, he told me that unless I hit him, that Serb, then all of them would beat me. Then I hit lightly. I just slapped him lightly in the face. Then the guard who was there, he slapped me with all the strength he could summon and told me, "That's how you should beat him".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that Serb later moved to another cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, first after me, my colleague also hit him and then he was transferred to another cell where Dzavid Mahmuljin was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened in that cell that you could hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could hear these provocations by that Serb who was provoking Dzavid Mahmuljin and I think he hit him or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So when the Serb was moved to the next cell, he was then obliged to attack the Muslim in that cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next day were you taken to the Prijedor SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point while you were in the Prijedor police station, did someone threaten to execute you and the other Muslims you were with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was Cigo who was there who threatened us. He said he wanted to have us shot. Then the guard came who was with us and said, "Don't shoot them. They will be shot where they are going".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The translation we received said, "They will be shot where they are going". Were those the words that the guard used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I guess that is not ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You get back to the same again ---

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- so I do not know you can correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the guard indicate you would be shot with a gun or that you would be in some way killed where you were going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "Where they are going, that is where they will be killed". He did not specify the manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt for a moment? Can I take up that matter of the redaction I mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, you can give us -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was at 12.06.42 and it appears in the transcript at page 23 line 21.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to that ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- redaction. OK, that redaction will be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Kenjar, after you were told at the Prijedor SUP that you would be killed where you were going, were you and the others then taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In Omarska were you first held in the small garage for a couple of days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a few days I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then were you held in the hangar building, in the upstairs portion of the hangar building for another couple of days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, again several days until that room was filled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then where were you moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we were moved to the ground floor, to the small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the small room near the room which leads to the stairway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in that room until you were transferred -- did you remain held in that room until you were transferred to Manjaca on August 6th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar how would you describe the general conditions in Omarska during the time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were disastrous conditions. They were not for living. They treated us like animals there. In a civilized world you do not treat animals like that. We did have not drinking water. The water that we had was contaminated. There was lice. People were called out day and night and taken out and never came back. There was a lot of abuse, a lot of provoking. In all kinds of ways we were abused. We were beaten during lunch time. We were forced to luncheon within three minutes and it looked impossible. Many would just leave their meals and would just take their bread with them. Sometimes they would get a quarter of bread, sometimes an eighth sometimes. They would be left without lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners called out from the rooms ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- for such purposes as interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the condition of the prisoners who returned from interrogation most often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners also called out from the rooms sometimes during the day and at night for beatings or killings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that happen on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every once in a while. Well, in fact daily. It happened every day. There was not a day passed that somebody was not taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you aware who the commander of the camp was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him around the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he see the condition of the prisoners who were beaten and treated in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course he did. He walked around on a daily basis. He was going to the white house where people were beaten up. He was probably seeing all the dead bodies around the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you involved in an effort to get someone released from the white house by getting bribe money to Meakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much money was asked for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were asking for 100 deutschemarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much money were you and the others able to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 100 francs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was the person you were trying to get released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hase Icic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Despite the fact that you were not able to collect the amount demanded, did that money prove sufficient to get Mr. Icic out of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you participate in collecting the money and then give it to another prisoner who gave it to Meakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, did you ever see Dule Tadic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that occur on the day that Jasko Hrnic was called from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day was it that you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an hour or maybe half an hour before he was taken out, before Jasko Hrnic was taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on that improvised hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And where was Dule Tadic when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was between those two canals in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, I am not sure if the cameras will permit us to see this as well as we might want, but I would wonder if you would indicate on the model, using that pointer to the right, where you were when you saw Dule Tadic and where he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was around here somewhere and Tadic was around there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please ask the witness to speak into a microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, get these microphones and put them on, please, and then speak into this microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot see it quite well. Do you mind if I walk nearby so I can see it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you can move over this way, if it is possible. Mr. Kenjar, if you can move this way. Can he, Mr. Tieger, you know better than I? Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, I am sorry to ask you to do this again, but if you could point out once again where you were first when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you indicate where he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So he was in an area between the two canals which are closest to the exit or entrance of the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was right around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might step forward for just a moment?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. To the model?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you need to join Mr. Tieger? OK, he just wanted to see better himself. Are we finished with Mr. Kenjar describing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Mr. Kenjar, you can resume your seat. Mr. Kenjar, when you saw Dule Tadic on that occasion what was he wearing, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he clean shaven or did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a few days growth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you absolutely sure that it was Dule Tadic that you saw at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, I am certain. He was close enough so that I could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you saw and recognised it was Dule Tadic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I turned around and I ran off to the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you actually run or did you walk quickly back to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not running. I just sped up. It would have been too conspicuous had I been running.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go back to your normal place in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I returned to there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we call up on the monitor Z3 19-33? I am advised we will have to use the Elmo. Our technician is not available. May I have Exhibit 256 then placed on the Elmo? I am sorry, I will have to have this marked for identification as Exhibit 256. Mr. Kenjar, do you recognise what is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that be tendered for admission and placed on the Elmo.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 256 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, although it is not shown in this portion of the photograph, is there a portion of the room where there is a small corner toward the front where the wall moves to the left and then expands the room slightly and moves back? Perhaps that is not a very good explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is such a part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you indicate on the photograph approximately where that would be located, although not shown in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of this blue table here. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked for identification, please, as Exhibit 257?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, could you indicate in the floor plan submitted by Miss Hollis where this particular room is, Exhibit 130A? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I did. I can certainly indicate. Would you like me to have the witness indicate on the model first or are you comfortable this way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Anything will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It will be A17, as indicated on Exhibit 130A. Mr. Kenjar, did you recognise what is in that photograph and does it show that portion of the room to which you were just referring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this photograph as Exhibit 257.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have we seen that, 257? We are looking at -- thank you, Mr. Wladimiroff. I have not seen it. We have the floor plan and we could see the kind of a cut in the room, but why do you not put it on the monitor. That does not give us -- yes, it does right there. Could you point, Mr. Kenjar, where the room comes out? Is that where the blue table is there and then it goes off to the left, I guess, from the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, as we look at that photograph is the entrance to the room to the left and the rear of the room to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would the direction of the entrance to the room as we are looking at the photograph be to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And would the back of the room be to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part where the table is, that is to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So as you enter the room the part that we are looking at now would be to the left, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is exactly right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 257?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 257 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have Exhibit 130A placed on the Elmo, please, 130A? Mr. Kenjar, looking at this exhibit and looking -- you may have to look at the actual exhibit to your right to make it out -- can you see the room marked A17? You may want to look to your right. I see it is not so clear on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, and does that show the room in which you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is showing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out on the actual exhibit to your right where your place in the room was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the exhibit).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be up there near that corner which we saw on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Jasko Hrnic, where was his normal place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that table, on top of that table, which was in that part of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked as Exhibit 258 for identification, please? Looking at this photograph, Mr. Kenjar, does this more closely resemble the table on which Jasko Hrnic was than, for example, the desk which is shown in the previous photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly that table.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this exhibit for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you put it on the Elmo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection ----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- to 258? 258 is what, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is the photograph of the table or a table which looked like the one on which Jasko Hrnic was sleeping.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. 258 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
