utterances.text: Why was Jasko Hrnic sleeping on the table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten up, so it was a more comfortable place for him. When he moved to our room he was beaten up. He was in a disastrous state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where had Mr. Hrnic been before he came to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was caught in Benkovac and then he was in a small garage and then he was moved to our room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Jasko Hrnic a well-known and popular person in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was known and he was quite popular.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of person was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. Why was he popular? What kind of person was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He drove motor cycles, big motor cycles. He had his own trucks. He was quite well known because of that and he was a good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Jasko Hrnic and Dule Tadic know each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they knew each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Could I just enquire about the first name of this man? Is that a nickname?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Was Jasko Mr. Hrnic's nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what his real name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasmin Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes see Dule Tadic and Jasko Hrnic associating together in Kozarac in cafes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, occasionally I would see them sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also know Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were he and Jasko Hrnic good friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners sometimes able to move from one room to another during the day depending on the shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For example, would it also be helpful if you were friendly with the person who was designated to interact with the guards and let people know when they could use the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you, for example, friendly with the person in your room or close to the person in your room who interacted with the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to visit other portions of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now did Emir Karabasic come to visit Jasko Hrnic in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was coming. He was visiting and also Jasmin was going to Emir Karabasic. They were friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you returned to the room after seeing Dule Tadic, did you go back to your normal place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that relative to the table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the table at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you tell Jasko Hrnic that you had seen Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did he react?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could see a fear in his eyes. His chin shivered and he was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now after approximately an hour to half an hour did prisoners begin to be called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they started to be called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember the precise order in which prisoners were called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was called out first, as you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was Emir's room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first floor above us. In a room directly above us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were you able to hear after Emir was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could hear screams and wailing and blows with blunt objects. You could hear all kinds of things. It was something terrible. It was like a nightmare.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30. (1.00 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjournment) (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. MR. ARMIN KENJAR, recalled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, before we adjourned, you were describing the sounds you heard after Emir Karabasic was called out from his room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sometime after that happened did you hear another prisoner called out from his room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What name was that who was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How was Jasko called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, he was called out as Asko Hrnic. I, we understood that they were calling out Asko Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, would you pull the microphone up a little bit? That might be better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During this incident were any other prisoners other than Emir Karabasic and Jasko Hrnic called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean in that room in which I was?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, no, during the incident as it occurred, were other prisoners, any other prisoner, besides Emir Karabasic and Jasko Hrnic called out, as you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear that. It is possible that some were called out but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know who Enver Alic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was called out during this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was called out too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall whether or not he was called out before or after Jasko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Jasko, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When Jasko Hrnic was called out as "Asko", did he go out right away, did he respond?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he called out more than once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We heard Asko Hrnic being called out, but I cannot remember, perhaps it was several times, we heard it once at that place where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Jasko finally respond or say anything to the calling out of his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only when the door opened, then Jasko said, "There is Jasmin Hrnic here, there is no Asko Hrnic", and then the individual who was in the doorway, in front of the door, he said, "It's you we need".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From the position you were in, were you able to see the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you select that spot for a particular reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were hiding, so to speak. We moved away behind that wall which covered us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that in part because you had been a Muslim reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was hiding. I did not want to be conspicuous.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What percentage of Muslim reserve policemen survived Omarska, would you estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A small percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Jasko finally go out at that point you described, after he had said, "There is Jasmin here"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Jasko went out, what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could hear screams, blows with some blunt instruments, cries of pain. One could hear noise. One could hear cry outs, "Bite to the balls", "Give it a blow", horrible, obscene expressions. It was the most terrible things I have yet lived to hear. I cannot wish it on anyone. That was really horrible. It was like a nightmare. I do not know what was happening with those people, what was happening to them, but I think they must have been massacred, killed, slain in the worst way possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did this continue for? Were there just a few screams, a few blows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite a long time, quite a long time. I felt it was an eternity, that it was a dream that would never end. It was so dreadful, so horrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the screams and the shouting and horrible and obscene expressions finally stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. Did all of this which you were listening to, the screams and the cries, finally end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did come to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sometime after that what could you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we heard the sound of the engine of that small TAM truck that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the TAM truck used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It served to bring food in and to take the bodies that were there out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you heard the engine of the small TAM truck, what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, then there was music. One could not hear properly, and after a while we again heard the sound of an engine, and the departure of that small TAM truck which had come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a short, after a short while, a shot could be heard from a distance, and I believe that one of them was still alive and, therefore, was finished up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After some period of time following this, did a guard come to the door and tell people they could again leave the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did someone leave the room and then come back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Asim Dergic came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When he came back, did he indicate that there was a need for some paste for washing, paste of the type that was used for washing the hands, in the WC?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he told me to take this paste to the WC, to room G, which was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go to the WC?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I took the paste and I went to that part in front of the WC where those troughs were, and there I saw person G with his head covered in some oil, some black oil, he had on the hair. I asked him what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he answered, "Don't ask". He was scared stiff. He looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the entrance to the WC, what did you see on the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw stains of freshly washed blood that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, after you returned to your room again and the incident was over, did you want to make some remembrance of your friend, Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after some time I sat at that table where Jasko used to sit and I reflected and I thought, well, Jasko is gone, he is no longer among us, and I turned and then I wrote on the wall, "18th June, 1900 hours".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we call up Z3 58-8? (To the witness): Mr. Kenjar, looking at the photograph which is now shown on the screen, does that indicate in the lower right hand or in the right hand portion of the photograph the date you wrote on the wall in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is written next to the date "June 18th" just to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "1900 hours".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that the time you wrote this down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the time when I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how long after the incident was over did you write it down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The name "Jasko" which is written to the left of that date, do you know who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was Jasko, that was -- he did it in his own hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The date which is written above, do you know what that date refers to specifically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not. Jasko perhaps recorded the birthday of his child or something else. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Or possibly the date he came to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly. I do not think so. I do not think -- I somehow think it was not the birthday of his son. I think the birthday came later. It could be the date of his arrival in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Jasko often writing the birthday of his son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all over the place, on the floor, on that table, on the walls. He talked about his son a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender the photograph as Exhibit 259.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 259 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, the first matter I want to ask you deals with your experiences during the conflict in general. How long were you in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 70 days, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: After that you went to another camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until December 13th '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does it mean, how many days or months or weeks were you in that other camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not count the days. I was not in such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But, anyhow, in December 1992 you left that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told us also this morning what happened to you before your arrival in Omarska, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: These were exceptional events you had never experienced before and in 1992 you were about 22, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have any opportunity to share all these terrible experiences with others, like relatives or friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the second part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have any opportunity to share all these terrible experiences with others, talking about it with your relatives or talking about it with your friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I take it -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was trying to forget it, to erase it, not to think about it. I talked very little about it, hardly with anyone. I would still probably not talk about it if I were not here. It is not something that I care about to remember that camp and all those crimes that took place there. I do not want ever to remember it, and after all this I shall try to forget it, not to recollect it, not to remember those events and everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Kenjar, that you are a little bit hesitant to share your experiences with others, but I take it that by not talking about it you may have been interested in reports about those camps and films so your suffering was acknowledged because others reported about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. When I happened to hear some stories about those camps, I think it would remind me of it so that I avoided any contact with people who talked about that camp. I avoided those talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You may have seen reports on television or even films about those camps. Have you seen those reports or have you ever seen those films that recognised those sufferings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, no. I avoided always to watch these events, since I had been through that all. I simply did not want to watch it and be reminded of them, of those horrors. I wanted to wipe it out from my memory. I do not want to be reminded of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever heard about the Monika Gras film on Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Knowing Tadic well, as you said, Mr. Kenjar, you must have seen his pictures in newspapers, magazines, on television, when he was arrested up to the broadcasting of this trial, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you discuss with others how Tadic looks and how he walks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you see other witnesses at the hotel where you stay now for this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, in your evidence you told us about an incident at the Orthodox church in Kozarac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told us that you heard about the incident and that you looked it up in the log book at the Kozarac police station, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and that would be an incident which would be noted down in that log book. It was not -- it was a report of what happened then and who went out to investigate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When did you hear about that incident before you looked it up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about it afterwards, afterwards, and then I leafed the log book later on in the evening when I was along while others were asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What do you know mean by "afterwards"? Could you give us a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, later that night. That night while I was on duty in front of the police station, I spent one hour outside and one hour inside, and during that hour that I spent inside I leafed through the books that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am not referring to the books, Mr. Kenjar, I am referring to the moment you heard about the story. Could you give us a date of that moment when you heard about that incident before you looked it up in the log book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that at all, the date I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you tell us the month you heard about that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot. I know it was summer, summer time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that long or shortly before the incident, the attack on Kozarac I mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think a short time, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who told you about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A friend of mine. There was talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who was that friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Saban Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Why did he tell it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were having a conversation about it and he mentioned that it was something in this regard, but he did not tell me a lot. He did not dare say more because that book was top secret, I mean, what was noted down in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am not referring to the book, Mr. Kenjar. I am referring to the moment that you were told. Did he tell you why he told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something as we were talking, I cannot really remember what we were talking about, and he mentioned it, to verify it later, for me to verify it later, to see whether it was true, to look in the book, in the log book, to see what was going on. I was interested in what was noted down there several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did your friend witness the events himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so but maybe yes, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So he told you what he was told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was simply telling me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When did you look it up in the log book, the same day or later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that on the same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that the next day or the same day that you were told about that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was later on, sometime had elapsed between.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: At what time did you hear about the incident from your friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about it sometime before I looked up the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I understand. Could you give us a time? Was it in the morning, in the afternoon or in the evening that you heard about the story from your friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you look in the log book the same evening or the evening of the next day?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered at least twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I did not get an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not think you have got an answer yet. May I help you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: See if we can at least get it straight. A friend, Mr. Jaskic, told you about this incident, is that correct, Mr. Kenjar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. He mentioned something. He told me nothing in detail what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then after your friend told you about the incident did you look it up in the log book to see if the incident had been recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some time after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How long after your friend told you about it did you look it up in the log book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. It could have been a week or even maybe two when it occurred to me and I was alone, I was thinking and I remembered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You were arrested on May 29th, was it, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So it must have been before then, is that correct, that you looked it up in the log book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Wladimiroff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. When you looked it up in the log book, did you read the day of the entry in that log book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not think so. I may have but I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was it a short entry, just a few lines, or a longer entry, more lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A short note -- nothing long.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was it on one page or was it on two pages, a part on one page and another part on the other page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a small portion of that book where one recorded all the things. It is a notebook, 60 by 40, quite a largish book, and it was a very small section, very small portion, of the book which recorded that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So I take it it was not one page, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on one page and there were also other entries there, but these entries were all very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was it on the left page or on the right page, Mr. Kenjar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I think it was on the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If located where it was, you do not know the date of the entry. Do you remember what was in the entry, what the entry said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So what did it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That Dusko Tadic was observed somewhere near the church with the probable intent of setting the church on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You are sure, nothing else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am sure -- well, there may have been something else but it was very short and that was what was written down about who was there that evening or day, that evening, whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know who made the entry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you seen any follow-up of that incident, that is, for example, a report to the priest of that church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no reports there. The reports were not entered in that book. Reports were written separately and submitted to the Commander, to Osme.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, in your evidence this morning you told that you were arrested after the takeover of Kozarac in a place called Mostanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What is that place, a village or a hamlet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a hamlet, a village, or near the monastery in Mostanica, that is where I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever been there before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does that village have streets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a chance to get into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where were you arrested then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the very entrance of Mostanica, at a monastery near the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that on a street or on a road or in a field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It was a road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a Macadam road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How far is Mostanica away from Bosanska Dubica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, maybe about two or three kilometres, not far.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So Mostanica is a different place to Bosanska Dubica, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, something like that, but it is all Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever been before in Bosanska Dubica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is Mostanica a village that is a part of Bosanska Dubica or is it, as a matter of fact, a separate village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is something like a part of a village. Until then I was never there, and when I was there it was not for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Let us move to Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told us that you were held in the hangar building and later on you moved to a smaller room at the ground floor, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. First, I was in a room on the top floor and then I was moved to the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: A room, as you describe, near to the stairway. Later this morning the Prosecutor told the Judges the number of that room before he asked you about it. Do you remember the number the Prosecutor passed to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was that number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Your Honours, I will pass a plan of the model in front of you without numbers. I would like the usher to show that plan to the witness and pass a copy to the Prosecutor. It is, as a matter of fact, a copy of 130A without numbers. I have another copy, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is the number? Defence Exhibit what for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: D23. Would you please look at that plan and then ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: -- put it on the Elmo on your right hand, please? Mr. Bos will assist you. Could we have the whole plan on the monitor, please? Thank you. Mr. Kenjar, could you point out on the Elmo on your right hand your room on that plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the plan) This one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Could you write a "K" in that room on that plan with a pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a while ago, Mr. Kenjar, you were shown an exhibit that showed the name of Jasko on the wall. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told us that you wrote the date of 18th June on that wall, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told us that you wrote that date 18th June one hour after the event, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So I take it that the event you were referring to took place on 18th June, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You were referring to what you heard, screaming and all that, and what you saw that day, that is, Dusko Tadic as you testified, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you were referring to the incident, you were referring to the incident related to Jasko Hrnic, is that correct, what you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And that was also the same day you saw Dusko Tadic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you if you had seen Dusko Tadic in Omarska on June 16th 1992, you confirmed -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection. That question was not asked.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We may look into our notes again. As far as I noted it down, the date was put to the witness and the witness confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I must admit, I do not recall. I will confer with the other Judges. I recall him saying that he saw him in the hallway outside of room A17.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is correct and, as a matter of fact, the Prosecution suggested the date to the witness and the witness simply confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are saying that was June 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That was June 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, your Honour, we might rephrase it, if it takes too long to track down.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was going to attempt to find out if we could locate that, the question, to determine what date it was. I then wanted to ask you how important it was and then ask you how we might talk about the importance ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am quite satisfied, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- outside the presence of the witness, if you wish, or however you want to handle it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We may rephrase the question to avoid problems.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. MR. WLADIMIROFF (To the witness): Mr. Kenjar, again that date on the wall, 18th June, as you just testified a minute ago, that was the day on which the event took place, the date you also saw Dusko Tadic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So if any other date might have been put to you, that other date could not be right, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think that that is the date that is the correct one, that when I was writing it down, I asked somebody of the people who were there around me for that date. I asked them what date it was today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see what you saw on that day. You told us this morning that you saw Tadic while you were in the hallway, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Am I right then that you were not in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right. I was not there. When I saw him I was not in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Why were you in the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was going to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How far did you get on your way to the toilet before you returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind those cabinets that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you need any permission to leave your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at that time the movement was permitted. We could move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there anyone standing at the doorway of your room to guard that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you think -- what do you mean, was there somebody armed who was there or somebody from our own?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there a guard, not someone of your own, standing at the door guarding that room or standing outside to guard that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you simply pass that person without explaining what you were going to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you could simply walk out of your room and go as you please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to the toilet and back. That part of the hangar, all the rooms that were upstairs, I could not go up there and you could not -- you had to ask and you could go to the toilet sometimes, sometimes you could not. It depends on the shift, what shift it was, and how, what their mood was. It depended on their mood. Sometimes they would lock us up in a room, they would not permit us to go to the toilet or water. They would not allow anything. We had to be silent. We could not even talk or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who was standing outside the door on June 18th when you were leaving the room going for the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean from the guards?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember who it was from the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know whose shift it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he gave you permission or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The others were going out, so I went out too. I did not ask for any permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you leave the room by yourself, alone or were you together with someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went there alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was approximately the time you left that room for the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately, one hour, maybe half an hour, before everything that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I understand, but could you tell us the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot estimate. Maybe it was one hour or maybe it was half an hour, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How did you know the time? You did not have a watch, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately I knew. I knew -- after it was all over I asked what time it was and somebody said it was around 6.00 when the incident was over with Jasko and Emir. So that it was around 6 o'clock and so I thought that it could be an hour or half an hour before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Coming out of your room you walked into the hall and then, as you testified this morning, you saw Tadic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was he alone or was he with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just standing by himself, no one else you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was moving, he was coming from the direction of that door that were behind, behind his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What kind of door was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The doors over there. The big garage door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that door open or closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you please get yourself a pencil again, if there is one there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you write down on that plan next to you where you indicated the "K" how you left the room, just drawing on that original map on the right of you ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: -- on that machine, write down how you walked and where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: OK. Could you indicate where you saw Dusko Tadic on that map with a "T"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you also indicate with a "W" where the toilet is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I made a mistake. The toilet was next to those troughs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You put there a "W" and a "2" behind it, "W" and then a "2"? No, just leave it there. Thank you. You also told us this morning that you saw the person you called Dusko Tadic in uniform. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You had been with the police, had you not, as a reserve policeman before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You had been with the police as a reserve policeman before the incident, had you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So I take it you know the difference between a police uniform and a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What kind of uniform did Dusko Tadic wear that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camouflage military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you tell us the colours of that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camouflage uniform, one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But one more time again for my part, can you tell us the colours of that uniform, of that camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are mixed in green, blue, all kinds of colours, mixed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a police uniform of mixed colours in blue and grey, of a camouflage type?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did this person you called Dusko Tadic wear such a uniform in grey and blue or in those different colours you just described before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the one I have described before, the military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Dusko Tadic in such a uniform before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This morning you also told us that Tadic had a beard, a growth of a few days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, rather grown in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Dusko Tadic with such a beard before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, you told us about the prisoners that were called from their rooms and you told us that, first of all, Emir Karabasic was called. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where was Emir Karabasic when he was called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was on the top floor, I believe, in that room on that floor above us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you leave your room, the room you just indicated to us on the plan, was there a door or was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the exit of my room where I was?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. Was there a door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a door at the exit where you left the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that door usually open or closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes it was open and sometimes it was closed. It depended. In the evening it would be closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What did it depend on? What was the reason why the door was closed and when was the door open? What was the policy here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended on the shift that was outside there. It depended on the guards who were there. When something went on in the corridor, then the door would be closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you went to the toilet nothing was going on in the hall, so I take it the door was open, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when I saw Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing was going on. It was -- all was quiet, everything was quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you heard Emir Karabasic called, there was something going on on the first floor, was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, what do you say, the door was open or closed, the door to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was closed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just imagine yourself again walking out of your door walking to the stairs to the first floor. Are there doors to the stairway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was this door next to us which was a glass door painted red which was also closed at night and sometimes it was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you had to open that door before you could enter the stairway, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was mostly open but sometimes it was closed. It depended on the shift there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there the same policy, when incidents it was closed and otherwise it might be open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: On the stairway coming to the first floor, were there doors too or were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was one before, while we were still in this room upstairs, there were guards there, but afterwards they all came down to that hangar, and in that hangar there were guards, so that on the staircase there were no guards at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you any knowledge of the policy on the first floor, as far as doors are involved, that is, doors closed or doors open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have already said it -- I am repeating -- it depended on the shift that was there. Sometimes it was open, sometimes it was closed, and I passed there several times, I went out and the door was closed sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. So actually what did you hear when you say, "I heard Emir Karabasic called"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What did you hear? Can you repeat it for us? Can you tell us what you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard Emir Karabasic being called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you in your room on the ground floor heard what was said in front of the room of Emir Karabasic on the first floor, that is what you tell us, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the room then and in the room I heard Emir Karabasic called out, not in front of my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Later on you were asked by the Prosecution about Jasko Hrnic and you told us that he was called out too but he was in your room, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Later on you were asked about Jasko Hrnic. He was called too, but he was in your room, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody asked me anything. They were looking for Jasko Hrnic and nobody asked me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I said the Prosecution asked you today about Jasko Hrnic, and then you told that he was called out of his room too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then you were asked if you heard about others called out of the room and then you said, "I did not hear others called". Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not. They were calling out, they called out Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Later on, indeed, you told the Prosecution after he asked you that Enver Alic was called too, that is correct, but do you remember that you told him first that you did not remember that, that you did not hear others called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that I did not hear any others. I heard those three being called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Tell us then, where was Enver Alic, in which room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The same room what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So on the first floor too, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: He was called, as I understand ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: -- after Emir Karabasic was called and after Jasko Hrnic was called, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was called out after Emir Karabasic and Jasko Hrnic, Enver Alic was called out too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When Emir Karabasic was called, did you hear anything happen after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you think that an incident was going on then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When Jasko Hrnic was called from your room, I suppose you thought that it got worse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was like that all the time -- terrible, abnormal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So am I right to think that there was no doubt that your door must have been closed, the door of your room, as well as the door on the first floor because that was the policy, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door to our room was closed until they called out Jasko. Until they came to that door and then they opened the door and called out Jasko, and Jasko went out and the door closed again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: From your spot in the room you could not see the door, you could not see through the door into the hallway, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see. I saw the door when it was closed the first time. When it was opened, one could feel by the sound that the door was opening, and when Jasko was called out -- was called out to come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Kenjar, was the room behind the glass door which led to the stairway filled with prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was full up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about the stairs themselves, did prisoners fill those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were also full and there were one or two sitting or standing on each one of the stairs. Some perhaps could even lie down on the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not there were lockers in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the entrance, at the entrance to the stairway, there were cupboards, lockers on both sides. To the left and to the right there were lockers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there prisoners on those lockers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were, one or two -- as many as could fit in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When guards or soldiers wanted to call out prisoners who were upstairs, do you know whether or not they went into the room and through the prisoners and up the stairs to call those people out or call them out from the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they called out at the entrance door, and then it was transmitted by word of mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you something I did not ask you earlier. Do you see Dule Tadic in court today?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I object, your Honour. It does not arise from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, your Honour, if it is a matter of reopening, I will. Secondly, the question of who he saw was raised.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, the question of who he saw was raised. That is for sure. You asked him whether he saw Mr. Tadic, where he saw him, whether it was on 16th that Mr. Kenjar wrote the name, wrote the date, rather, regarding Mr. Hrnic and when was that in comparison to when he saw Mr. Tadic. That is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Absolutely, your Honour, as far as connected to a date but I did not raise the ID issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule your objection, Mr. Wladimiroff. Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Kenjar, again do you see Dule Tadic here in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out where he is, please, and tell us what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There. A green suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. May the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. The record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Judge Stephen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you a couple of questions about reserve police. What qualified you to be a reserve policeman? Were you selected in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know how it all went. I did not have any orders in case of war. I do not know in the army. I was with the blue ones, with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you particularly trained as a reserve police? I ask these questions because we have heard a lot about reserve policemen, you see? It is not particularly you that I am concerned with. Did you undergo some training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was a paid occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was paid, but I never received any salary because there were no salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For how long were you a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, for about five or six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What uniform did you wear as a reserve policeman? Was it the same uniform as the regular police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we had winter uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which was different from the regular police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, well, it was similar. I mean, regular police also had the same kind of uniforms, except that we had winter uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your powers? Were your powers of arrest, for instance, the same as those of the regular police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what way were they different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if we noticed something or found something or anyone, we were supposed to call the police station in Kozarac, to some active duty policemen who were there and then they would proceed with the whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Apart from your powers, what were your duties? Did you have specific times each day when you had to serve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had shifts, one, two and three. First, for the first two days, the first shift from 6.00 to 3.00, I believe, and then the second shift and then the third one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the role of reserve policeman one that was specially created for the emergency situation in former Yugoslavia or had there always been reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There always have been, but they were seldom activated, only in some extraordinary situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Therefore, during the months that you were a reserve policeman, that was during a time which needed the activation of reserve police, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have just a few questions, some of them related to the questions that Judge Stephen just asked. Then, I gather, Mr. Kenjar, you worked one of these shifts as a reserve police officer for five to six months, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you did not then continue to work as a carpenter during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have to report to the police station in Kozarac when you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had to do it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You would report to the police headquarters in Kozarac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and I worked. I never was absent from my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you actually work at the police office in Kozarac? Was that your assignment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in front of the police station taking care of the safety of the police station in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So your duties were to stay outside the police station in Kozarac for this five to six months, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was -- the time was shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Shorter? Shorter than five to six months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was not there all the time. I spent a shorter period of time in front of that police station. It was only that I was there from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever work inside the police office or police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, except during breaks when I would be -- well, yes, I spent one hour outside and then one hour inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the name of this book that you saw the notation regarding the incident at the Serbian Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a log book, it is called Knjiga Prijava. It was a large book that was always there on the table by the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why do you say it was top secret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there were all sorts of records in there of various complaints in order to preserve the identity of the guilty party or, rather, of the plaintiff, in order to preserve the identity of the person who, whatever, filed a complaint or whatever. It was secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a particular person responsible for making entries in this book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the person on duty in the police station, he was the one who took down those notes and they also worked in three shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So whoever was on duty for that particular shift was responsible for making the entries regarding potential criminal incidents, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw it during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you left Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Before Omarska, before my arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what has happened to that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It used to be on the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You do not know where it is now, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just one, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The other part of your duties with the reserve police involved traffic control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Again nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any objection to Mr. Kenjar being permanently excused, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kenjar, you are permanently excused. That means that you may leave and you are free to leave at this time. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess now for 20 minutes. Unless there is a matter we can consider, we would rather start with the witness when we return. Very good. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (3.54 p.m. (The Court adjourned for a short time) (4.15 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call the next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The next witness is Mehmed Alic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you wish to offer into evidence Defence Exhibit 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. You are perfectly right, your Honour. I forgot to tender it. I may tender it, if you please, as marked.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection to Defence 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are thinking that it is too late now because the witness has gone though! This is just clean up, if I say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you say so.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Defence Exhibit 23 will be admitted. I notice there has been a change in the order for the witnesses. Is that correct? Am I reading the change in the order correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Defence knows that? Very good. Sir, would you please take the oath that is before you? Mehmed Alic, called

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, will you first state your name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alic Mehmed, son of Aga.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic in what year were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 27th March 1923.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Kamicani, in the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you live there your whole life until the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, until 1992 we lived there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your occupation in Kam icani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a farmer and over time I also worked with a forest. I was doing forestry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you raise a family in Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had a wife and six children, spouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, there was Hatemina, Enver, Envera, Sedika, Ekrem and Nasiha.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The translation did not come out clearly. One of your sons' names was Enver and your daughter's name was Envera, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Ekrem's nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Aka".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is my fault. What was Enver's nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Eno".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what years were Enver and Ekrem born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Enver was born in 1948 and Ekrem in 1955.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were their occupations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were both drivers, one, Enver, worked in Croatia in a company and the other one worked with me because I had a tractor and I had a truck and I also had horses and so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, did you know the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know his father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the two of you of approximately the same generation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was his father's name? If you do not recall, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know, but now, right now, it has just slipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sure you are a bit nervous, I understand. How well did the two of you get along, Dule Tadic's father and yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he knew me quite well. When I went to the forest he used to, in front of his house, he would lean against the fence and if I am going there in the morning, he would say, "Good morning", and he said, "How are you?" and I always had good horses, so he would say, "Nice horses" and he said, "Oh, you are hard working".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that typical of relations between Serbs and Muslims during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were either of your sons about the same age as Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Ekrem was born in 55, my Ekrem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Ekrem or Enver know Dule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both knew him. Of course, they all would drink together at the same table and went to music and all kinds of places.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Have you known Dule Tadic ever since he was a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about some of the things that happened after the attack on Kozarac. First of all, do you recall when that began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attack started on 24th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home in Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there with my wife and my daughter and my granddaughters, grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the outbreak of the attack, did you and the members of your family go to Mujici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went first to Softici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that did you go on to Mujici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then to Mujici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in Mujici until May 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until May 26th, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On that day in the morning did you and the other members of your family go with other ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We started towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that in order to surrender to Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you travel to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The older people and the children, we took tractors and we would put on the older people and children and women and we would go in a tractor to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the younger and stronger go on foot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The younger and the stronger went on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you reached Kozarac, did you and the other elderly people get off the tractors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did columns of people form in Kozarac to move through the town for the purpose of surrendering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that going down Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In Kozarac were you put on a bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Krkici, down at Krkici, we, elderly, and the children and women, we got on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that one bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were in the first bus and then I was not really looking any more. There was one bus there at that time and then afterwards others came, but I was in the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is Krkici where the junction where the old road meets Marsala Tita?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the bus on which you and the other elderly were put proceed with the column of people on foot to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In which direction was the column going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It went towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the column stop at some point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Susici near Limenka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
